historical_references.reference: Biplob was a revolutionary leader who led an unsuccessful rebellion against the British rule in Bengal in 1857.
historical_references.context: Biplob led the Indigo rebellion in Bengal, which was triggered by the excessive taxation of indigo farmers by the British East India Company. Biplob is considered one of the earliest Indian freedom fighters who inspired later revolutionaries like Tantu Mian and Mangal Pandey.

historical_references.reference: Biplob was also a prominent revolutionary leader during the Swadeshi Movement in early 20th century Bengal.
historical_references.context: Biplob was a key figure in the Swadeshi Movement, which was a nationalist movement aimed at promoting indigenous goods and boycotting foreign goods in response to the British-imposed partition of Bengal in 1905. Biplob and other leaders like Aurobindo Ghosh and Lala Lajpat Rai played a significant role in organizing protests and violence against the British.
